## Which language do you use most for data analysis?

::: {.poll #lang}
- R
- Python
- Julia
- Something else
:::

## What is the capital of Australia?

::: {.poll #capital}
- [ ] Sydney
- [x] Canberra
- [ ] Melbourne
- [ ] Perth
:::

## In between questions

An ordinary slide. With `close-on-leave` (the default), arriving here
closes the question on the previous slide, so late votes are rejected.

Phones keep showing the closed question's results until the next one opens.

## One word for today's lecture?

::: {.wordcloud #mood max-words=2 max-answers=3}
:::

## Before the reveal

::: {.poll #pvalue results="hidden"}
A p-value of 0.03 means:

- [ ] There is a 3% chance the null hypothesis is true
- [x] Data this extreme would occur 3% of the time if the null were true
- [ ] There is a 97% chance the result is real
:::

## How did today go?

::: {.likert #feedback scale="agree-5"}
- The pace of today's lecture was right
- The examples helped
- I could follow the live coding
:::

## How confident are you running a t-test in R?

::: {.likert #confidence scale="0-10" low="Not at all" high="Completely"}
:::

## How was the pace?

::: {.likert #speed labels="Too slow|Just right|Too fast"}
- Pace of today's lecture
:::

## Presenter keys

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `Q` | Full-screen QR code for everyone to scan |
| `A` | Reveal the correct answer (also closes voting) |
| `T` | Show or hide results on this slide |

Open the deck once with `?presenter=<key>` to take control; the key is
remembered in this browser and removed from the address bar. Without it the
deck is a read-only viewer. Press `?` for all reveal.js shortcuts.
